title: Stage 4: Reporting views
summary: Give the dashboard stable, named queries: monthly revenue and customer value.

steps.title: Views as the reporting layer
body: The dashboard shouldn't know about surrogate keys and joins. Give it **views** with friendly names and exactly the columns it shows. When the model changes, you fix the view, and the dashboard keeps working.

Views can contain anything a SELECT can: joins, GROUP BY, window functions. For heavy reports on big data, warehouses *materialise* them into tables on a schedule; at Inkwell's size a plain view is instant.

CREATE TABLE stg_orders ( order_ref TEXT NOT NULL, order_date TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL, customer_name TEXT NOT NULL, isbn TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0), unit_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (unit_cents >= 0), channel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('web', 'shop')), PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, isbn) );

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO stg_orders (order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel) SELECT trim(order_ref), CASE WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN substr(order_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(order_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(order_date, 1, 2) ELSE order_date END, lower(trim(customer_email)), trim(customer_name), trim(isbn), trim(title), CAST(trim(qty) AS INTEGER), CAST(ROUND(CAST(replace(trim(unit_price), '£', '') AS REAL) * 100) AS INTEGER), lower(trim(channel)) FROM raw_orders;
CREATE TABLE dim_customer (customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE dim_book (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, title TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO dim_customer (email, name) SELECT DISTINCT email, customer_name FROM stg_orders;
INSERT INTO dim_book (isbn, title) SELECT DISTINCT isbn, title FROM stg_orders;

CREATE TABLE fact_sales ( order_ref TEXT NOT NULL, order_date TEXT NOT NULL, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_customer(customer_id), book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_book(book_id), channel TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL, revenue_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, book_id) );

INSERT INTO fact_sales SELECT s.order_ref, s.order_date, c.customer_id, b.book_id, s.channel, s.qty, s.qty * s.unit_cents FROM stg_orders AS s JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.email = s.email JOIN dim_book AS b ON b.isbn = s.isbn;

steps.title: v_customer_value
prompt: Create the view **`v_customer_value`** with one row per customer and columns **name**, **email**, **orders** (distinct orders), **revenue_cents**, and **value_rank** (`RANK()` by revenue, highest = 1).
Tables: `dim_customer(customer_id, email, name)`, `dim_book(book_id, isbn, title)`, `fact_sales(order_ref, order_date, customer_id, book_id, channel, qty, revenue_cents)`.
solution: RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(f.revenue_cents) DESC) AS value_rank
JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.customer_id = f.customer_id

steps.title: Channel mix
prompt: Using **only the views**, return each **month** with **web_cents**, **shop_cents** and **web_pct** (web's share of the month's revenue, rounded to the nearest whole number), in month order.
solution: COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN channel = 'web' THEN revenue_cents END), 0) AS web_cents,
COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN channel = 'shop' THEN revenue_cents END), 0) AS shop_cents,
ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN channel = 'web' THEN revenue_cents END), 0) / SUM(revenue_cents)) AS web_pct
